text:
jonah: quick share from the region kernel sweep — ran flashv3 vs triton/cuBLAS across h100/a100 in us-east and eu-west for the new 16k model. linking charts: https://files.redwood/internal/bench/2956789012 (p95/p99 + qps)
rachel: looked at the charts — interesting tail in eu-west for flashv3 at small payloads/high QPS. p99 spikes ~420ms vs us-east ~220ms, p95 ~120ms.
maria: that matches the microburst warmup we saw last month. small requests cause packing jitter, flashv3 kernel start costs seem higher in eu-west because of driver version drift.
jonah: agreed. numbers:
- us-east h100 flashv3 qps=1200 p95=85ms p99=210ms throughput ok
- eu-west h100 flashv3 qps=1100 p95=118ms p99=420ms
- eu-west h100 triton/cuBLAS qps=1050 p95=110ms p99=240ms
sam: also ran q8 quant tests — eu-west flashv3 q8 p99 jumps to 520ms, triton q8 p99=260ms. seems quant + flashv3 combo amplifies tail.
aj: thanks. do we think it's kernel-level (startup/aten calls) or infra (driver mismatch, clock governor)?
maria: likely both. vendor libs (cuBLAS/cuDNN) get lower startup overhead for small-latency paths on our driver stack in eu-west. flashv3 shines for long sequences and packing efficiency.
lee: proposal: adaptive routing by payload shape + hysteresis. quick rule sketch:
```yaml
kernel_selection:
  - if seq_len <= 256 and payload_bytes < 8k: prefer vendor
  - if seq_len > 1024: prefer flashv3
  - else: choose by dynamic score (latency_cost + token_cost)
hysteresis_ms: 50
cooldown: 300s
```
rachel: +1 to hysteresis. also add a region override table for eu-west to bias vendor until driver rollouts complete.
jonah: good. ops question: do we flip the default for all EU hosts or do a canary? prefer staged.
deploy-bot: canary rollout created: kernel-routing-policy v0.3 -> 10% eu-west. rollout id=c-295678. started.
aj: also recommend we run a targeted warmup shot for microbursts: pre-warm small kernels for 30s bursts to prime SMs and cache.
maria: warmup scripts looked like this (simple curl loop):
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/serve/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}' &
  sleep 0.5
done
```
sam: i'll run warmup + quant q8 set on the canary hosts and post updated charts in ~45m.
lee: one more: add metric to track "kernel_fallback_rate" per region/payload so we can correlate with quality/regression alerts.
jonah: perfect. next steps: (1) run sam's warmup + q8 on canary (2) monitor p95/p99 and kernel_fallback_rate (3) adjust hysteresis/thresholds after 1h. if stable, ramp to 50% then full.
rachel: documenting expected regressions in the rollout note. also ping infra to check driver versions in eu-west tomorrow.
aj: FYI, if we need temporary safety net, we can force vendor kernel for production routes using route override: `kernel=vendor` at route level.
sam: update: initial warmup + q8 on canary looks promising — p99 down from 520ms -> 270ms after warmup. posting charts now.
maria: excellent. keep an eye on accuracy drift for q8 though, run eval set.
jonah: thanks everyone. will wait for sam's full graphs and then propose hysteresis numbers.
deploy-bot: canary rollout pct updated -> 10% (running).
